correctness.rationale: Every commutative bilinear law on F2^3 is uniquely one of 2^18 encoded six-output tables. The exhaustive C++17 checker tests all 64 x,y pairs, partitions every accepted law under all 168 invertible linear maps, and checks orbit coverage, least representatives, stabilizer divisibility, stratum invariance, weighted totals and three independent Burnside counts. It finds 2858/47 pointwise, 1898/32 scalar-extension-stable and 988/16 associative structures/classes. The formal coefficient proof establishes exact extension stability; a second direct F4 evaluation on every accepted table agrees, and an explicit F4 witness confirms non-stability of the example. Source and 47 canonical representatives are supplied; no extrapolation is made from finite samples.

originality.rationale: The October 2026 primary classification explicitly excludes the field with two elements. Its geometric analysis over algebraically closed characteristic-two fields does not enumerate rational-isomorphism orbits over F2. Hegazi–Abdelwahab addresses only nilpotent algebras; Cedilnik–Jerman only zeropotent; Cedilnik only isopotent. The complete 47-class pointwise census, 32-class extension-stable census and 15-class difference are not statements or consequences identified in those sources. Indexed result searches and accessible earlier claims revealed only complementary proper-subclass results; unindexed priority risk remains.
residual_risks: An unindexed finite-algebra table or historical classification might already list the 47 binary-field classes and the 32 scalar-extension-stable classes.

Some literature uses a quadratic-Jordan-algebra convention in characteristic two; this theorem deliberately classifies only the explicitly defined commutative-bilinear polynomial identity and its scalar-extension stability.
Some subfamilies are previously classified; novelty concerns the complete simultaneous orbit census and precise 15-class field-size boundary, not previously covered special cases.

value.rationale: This completes the exact smallest-field endpoint explicitly excluded from an October 2026 classification of three-dimensional Jordan algebras. The 15 pointwise-only isomorphism classes exhibit a mathematically substantive distinction between a polynomial identity on F2-points and the same identity over extensions; the full orbit representatives and automorphism orders make the classification usable for comparisons and descent calculations. A natural complete classification and structural field-boundary phenomenon qualify independently of generalizations to higher dimensions.
